question: Are exact repeated two-rune patterns at lag 13 in 15-rune within-page windows more frequent than page-composition-preserving shuffles?
source_scope: Archived LP2-00–55 rune-bearing page texts. Retain headings; exclude page-crossing windows and non-runes.
operational_rule: A 15-rune window beginning at i qualifies if C[i]=C[i+13] and C[i+1]=C[i+14]. This is one narrow interpretation of an unspecified reported 'recurring pattern'; no source coordinates were supplied.
window_lengths: Lengths 10-13 have no internal lag-13 pair; length 14 has one; length 15 has two. Only length 15 can contain this repeated two-rune pattern.
selection_control: For each lag 2-28, count exact repeated two-rune patterns on every eligible within-page window of length lag+2. Divide by its exact fixed-page-composition shuffle expectation. Compare the observed lag-13 count to 499 page-preserving shuffles; compare the best observed ratio across all 27 lags to each shuffle's own best ratio. The latter adjusts for choosing a lag after looking across this declared range, but not for all possible pattern rules.
excluded: Word boundaries, keys, skipped runes, marker rules, non-exact motifs, windows longer than 15 for the fixed-lag claim, and a cipher generator.
